pool.text: The first mention of the Kalikata village was found in Bipradas Pipilai's Manasa Vijay.
The British completed the construction of Fort William to protect their trading factory.
The first newspaper in India, the Bengal Gazette started publishing from the city.
Established as the nation's oldest museum, the Indian Museum houses large collections.
The Calcutta Medical College was founded as the first institution in Asia.
A typhoon struck the city and killed about 60,000 in Kolkata.
The Port of Kolkata was established as India's oldest river port.
Calcutta was host to the first national conference of the Indian National Association.
Millions starved to death during the Bengal famine due to multiple factors.
Demands for a Muslim state led to an episode of communal violence.
The city hosted the government-in-exile of Bangladesh during the war.
The Kolkata Metro became the oldest underground mass transit system in India.
Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi dubbed Kolkata a dying city.
The official name Calcutta was changed to Kolkata to match pronunciation.
The Calcutta High Court ruled that the city does not have a founder.
Cyclone Aila caused widespread damage to Kolkata with torrential rainfall.
Left Front was succeeded by the Trinamool Congress in the election.
The airport was upgraded to handle increased air traffic in the city.
The Kolkata Municipal Corporation was ranked first for best governance practices.
Part of the second line of the metro was inaugurated in the area.
